name: setup-wizard-3-step-compliance-index
title: Step 3: Compliance Index
description: The Compliance Index in develop's two phases. Build the index from every approved requirement, then shape it by hand (rename, lock, delete, drag, add) and re-run it with guidance typed to Aldo. Then one Draft run reads, files, merges and completes the actions and obligations, and a person reviews them a subcategory at a time: approve, discard, merge, edit, with Suggest subcategories for what fit nowhere. Every draft rests on step 2 requirement IDs that open the commitment as step 2 marked it up.

sections.label: No index yet
sections.html:
No index yet

Build it from 910 approved requirements.

guide.intent: Where step 3 starts: the three panes stand from the start, without data. The Index pane is empty but for its + Category and fold keys, Aldo's conversation is empty, and the center reads "No index yet" and how many approved requirements it builds from. Its keys are in the console: Build index and + Category. Build index runs ProposeComplianceIndex over every approved requirement and streams in the run console as it goes (the key reads Building until it lands; the center is blank meanwhile); + Category starts the index by hand.
decisions: A hand-made category or subcategory is locked from the start, as prod makes it, so a later Re-run leaves it alone.
acceptance: On a fresh step 3 the Index, center and Aldo panes all show, empty.
Build index streams in the run console for about 12 seconds, then shows the proposal: 17 categories and 75 subcategories.

sections.label: Console

guide.intent: The foot of the step's panel, as step 1 carries its scan console: the header carries no keys. A sunken tray across the panel under the header rule, every key neutral: Prev at its left end, Next at its right, the step's keys centered between, by phase. No index yet: Build index and + Category (no Prev or Next). Built: Re-run and Draft actions & obligations. During a run: the run's key, disabled. After it: Start over (the undo glyph), Draft again (its title names what is outstanding), Suggest Subcategories (while something fits no subcategory), View Log (the run's record in the console lightbox) and Approve All. Under the tray, once there is an index, every subcategory in index order, step 2's scrubber, a rule and the category's name where each category starts, a band of the category's hue along the foot of its cells and its name marked in the same hue. Drafted: darker gray for drafts never opened, light gray for opened with drafts to review, its category's hue once every draft is decided, so a finished index reads as the categories' colors. A dot at the top of a cell when the subcategory holds actions, and one at its foot when it holds obligations, so a cell carries one or two; each is dim while any of its drafts is left to review. No amber: nothing on the strip reads as alarm.
decisions: Reset the prototype, under the workspace as on step 1, starts step 3 over after a confirm: no index, no drafts, no talk with Aldo.
The strip is step 1's: 50 cells, 32px tall, the same gaps and the same color logic (light gray undecided, darker gray wants a look, the step's color done).

Start over is PR #1520's: once a Draft run exists it replaces Re-run, and it deletes the index and every draft back to "No index yet". Prod refuses it while a run is live or an approved record has evidence.
Approve All approves every pending draft after a confirm that counts the subcategories never opened. Draft actions with no scope stay drafts.
No position line and no Next to review: Prev and Next, or the arrow keys, step one subcategory at a time; the thumb is where you are.
Opened is not reviewed. Prod sets FirstOpenedDate the first time a bin with drafts is opened.

sections.label: Run console

guide.intent: Build index and the Draft run, each as a session. Build index is two tool calls: Read requirements streams each commitment read with its requirement count, and Propose index streams each category and subcategory proposed as a green + line with its citations; it ends on "Done in 12s." with the categories and subcategories to review, and View Log reopens it until the index is drafted. The Draft run: In the step panel it is a peek no taller than 100px: the newest lines of the stage running and the spinner, fading out at the top. Pressing it (or Open log) opens the console by itself in a lightbox over the page, its close key in the corner; Esc and a click outside also close it. When the run ends the peek goes and View log reopens the same lightbox. The key pressed is the prompt line. Each stage is a tool call: a dot (blinking while it runs, green when done), its name and what it works over ("910 requirements"). Under it, behind an elbow, what the run is doing to this project streams: the commitments read with their requirements and items, the subcategories filed into with their item counts and each item that fits none, each draft merged from more than one item with its requirement IDs, each action completed with its type, scope and responsible party. A done stage folds to its sentence ("2,463 of 2,473 items filed, 10 fit no subcategory") with Show N to unfold every line. Below the stages, a spinner names the stage in progress with elapsed seconds and its count, and the four stages tick off under it. The run ends on "Done in 26s." with the drafts filed and what needs attention. After a Re-run (built phase), the same console shows the guidance as the prompt and Propose index as a diff: + added, − removed, and bins kept because they are locked.
decisions: No percentage bar and no form dialog: the lightbox is the console alone, a thin border on a dimmed page. The count that moves is always a real noun (requirements, items, actions), and the lines are the drafts file's own: commitment codes, subcategory names, requirement IDs.
The console is the one dark surface on the page, in the --bcn-console-* tokens; every text tone clears 4.5:1 on its ground.
Warnings are amber lines in the stage that found them (an item that fits no subcategory, an action with no responsible party); requirements that bind nothing are a quiet line under Read requirements.
bcn-console is reusable: prompt, tool, row, spinner, todo and message are its whole grammar (console.ts).
acceptance: Pressing Draft actions & obligations opens the console with the prompt line and Read requirements streaming commitment codes; the spinner reads "Reading requirements…" with seconds and "N of 910 requirements".
The peek is at most 100px tall during a run; pressing it opens the full console in the lightbox, which keeps streaming until the run ends.
When the run ends the peek goes; View Log in the console opens the same record in the lightbox.
The lightbox is a terminal window's shape and one fixed size (50rem by 32rem, smaller on a small screen): it never grows as the log fills; the log scrolls inside it.
The demo runs at twice prod's pace (about 26 seconds for a full run) so it can be watched.
After a Re-run with guidance, added bins read as green + lines and removed bins as red − lines.

sections.label: Index
sections.html: Index

guide.intent: The sidebar, as develop keeps it. Category and subcategory rows with tools on hover: rename in place, lock or unlock, delete, drag within the parent; + Subcategory on a category; Expand all, Lock all and + Category over the tree. Each category has a hue, a dot on its row and its subcategories' rows. Once drafted, each subcategory carries develop's marks: a dot when it has drafts and was never opened, the count to review, a check when every draft is decided (muted when all were discarded). A category gets Approve category. Folded, the index is a rail that reads Index sideways, as the library and Aldo do.
decisions: Categories and subcategories only. Drafts are read on the subcategory's page, not listed in the index.
Row tools lie over the end of the row on hover, so the row never moves.
Renaming locks the row. Names are unique among siblings.
Locking a category locks its subcategories; unlocking it does not unlock them.
A bin that holds drafts is kept on Re-run; its lock is shown disabled with the reason.
Delete names what goes: items from N requirements go back to be filed on the next Draft run, and the drafts filed there are deleted. A bin holding approved actions cannot be deleted.

sections.label: Subcategory page
sections.html:
1. Category
  2. Subcategory

Discarded

guide.intent: One bar pinned across the top of the pane, as the PDF's page tools are on step 1: where it sits, Category › Subcategory as plain text (a header, not links), each with its color dot in the category's hue (as in the index and the scrubber), each cut to fit with the full name in its title; then Merge (off until two or more are ticked, then Merge (N)), Discard all and Approve all (N). In a pane under 720px, Merge and Discard all fold to their icons. No title in the document voice. Before drafting: the lists as develop renders them before a run fills them, Actions (0) and Obligations (0) each reading None, Approve all and Discard all disabled. Drafted: two lists, Actions then Obligations, then Discarded (N), folded, with Restore and Restore all. Each draft is one line: a box to tick for Merge, its kind chip, its title cut to the row, and its commitments as purple commitment badges. More than one commitment stacks left to right, the ones under it peeking out; pressing the stack opens a popover to its left listing every commitment with its title, each opening it. The title opens the draft's edit form in the side panel. Approve all (N) asks first; Discard all does not.
decisions: Review is by home subcategory only. Also filed in shows on the obligation, read only.
A draft action with no scope cannot be approved: "This draft has no scope. Set one before approving it."
Actions and obligations are the structure. Audience is a field on the obligation, not a grouping; sorting, filtering or grouping by it can come later as options.

Merge takes two or more drafts of one kind; when it cannot, its title says why. Obligations read by different people, or of different classes, merge: the dialog asks which Audience and Class the merged draft keeps (prod refuses different audiences). The merged draft keeps every source.
The header is esa-breadcrumbs with no links; its icon slot holds the dot, and the controller writes the names and the hue at run time.
Rationale is never stored or shown, as in prod.

Kind chips: an action is its requirement type (Plan, Reporting, Approval & Consultation…) tinted from the action hue; an obligation is develop's class chip (Adhere, Monitor, Notify, Roster) tinted from the class hue. Each list's kind column is as wide as its widest chip.
acceptance: Ticking two Compliance staff drafts in Take and injury reporting and merging them leaves 20 drafts where there were 21.

sections.label: Edit panel
sections.html:
DraftApprovedDiscarded

Sources

    Also filed in

guide.intent: A draft's edit form in the side panel, as develop's two edit dialogs carry it. The header names it (Edit obligation, or the action's name) with its status badge. An obligation: Title, Class, Audience, Applies when, Monitor signs (type one and press Enter), then its Sources (each requirement's commitment badge and name, and the words it rests on) and Also filed in. An action, in three tabs: Details (Name, Type, Responsible party, Scope, Action text), Timing (Frequency; one time: deadline milestone, offset, period and direction; recurring: every N periods between a start and an end milestone; as needed: the event that triggers it) and Evidence of compliance (Expected evidence), then its Sources. The footer: Approve and Discard (Restore on a discarded draft) at the left; Save and Cancel at the right.
decisions: The review's verdicts live in the panel because the row has no record of its own. In develop the subcategory pane holds them; the edit dialog in index mode has only Save and Cancel.
Approve saves the form first, so setting a scope and approving is one press.
Sources are read only: what a draft rests on changes only by Merge.
acceptance: Opening Take Contact Representative Notice shows Reporting, DWR, Project scope and one source, EC-1.

sections.label: Commitment panel
sections.html: Parsing

guide.intent: Where a locator leads: the commitment as step 2 marked it up, read only, the requirement in focus and the draft's excerpt a heavier pass inside it. The page key opens the PDF; Open in Commitments lands step 2 on that commitment.

sections.label: Aldo
sections.html:
Aldo

      Drop to attach

        Instructions in effect

guide.intent: One conversation per subcategory. Before drafting it takes Re-run guidance in plain words and answers with the Re-run key and what a re-run keeps; Re-run in the step's actions opens the same exchange. Drafted, it approves all, discards, merges two drafts (@ each), makes an obligation a monitor's duty, and says why a draft is here from its sources. Open items: a draft action with nobody named to do it, or no scope.
decisions: Guidance holds for one run and is not kept, as prod's.

One Re-run with guidance was run ahead through Beacon's prompt ("give each listed species its own subcategory under an Endangered Species category"). Other guidance gets a plain answer that offers it.

sections.label: Merge
sections.html:
Drafts

    Merged draft

guide.intent: Two columns. Left, the ticked drafts as they read, numbered: class, who reads it, title, Applies when (or an action's scope, party, frequency and deadline), and each requirement with its excerpt. Right, the merged draft as it will be made: the title, the first draft's fields, and every requirement and monitor sign of every draft, each marked with the numbers of the drafts it came from. Pressing a draft's title makes it the merged title; the title stays editable. Merge, then Cancel.
decisions: The preview is what merge() keeps: the union of requirements (one row per requirement and excerpt) and of monitor signs. That a merge loses no source is shown by the numbers on each row, not said.
The merged draft takes the first ticked draft's class, audience and Applies when, whichever title is picked; the preview shows it.
acceptance: Merging two Compliance staff drafts in Take and injury reporting shows Requirements (2) marked 1 and 2, and Monitor signs (4) on the merged draft.

sections.label: Suggest subcategories
sections.html:
Fits a bin you already have

    New bins

      Better left without a bin of their own

      Unfiled›Needs a home

guide.intent: Homes for what fit no subcategory, in develop's three parts: fits a bin you already have, new bins (named and placed), and better left without a bin of their own (Unfiled › Needs a home). Each suggestion is a card whose header is where its items land, as the index draws it: the category's hue dot, the category, ›, the subcategory. A new bin's header is that placement as two fields, Category then Subcategory, its dot following the category chosen. Under the header, the items as review rows: kind chip, statement, commitment badges. Better left without a bin of their own is one card, Unfiled › Needs a home, each item with its own tick and its reason under it. Unticking fades what Apply will leave out. Apply files them; Draft again makes drafts of them.
decisions: A suggestion is accepted whole, one tick a card; the plan already takes a subset, so per-item ticks are a later option.
Unfiled actions carry no requirement type yet, so their chip reads Action.
